summary.text: Dale Hamby is an independent candidate for Pennsylvania House of Representatives District 100 in the November 3, 2026 general election, facing Dave Nissley (R).
A retired U.S. Army officer who runs a sheep farm in southern Lancaster County, he previously ran for the seat as a Democrat in 2016 and 2018, according to Ballotpedia and his own survey response.

paragraphs.text: Hamby graduated from Black River High School and earned a bachelor's degree from the United States Military Academy at West Point in 1978, a second bachelor's degree from Roosevelt University in 1985, and a graduate degree from Harvard Business School in 1989.
He served in the U.S. Army from 1978 to 1993, and Ballotpedia lists his profession as farmer and businessman.
In his Ballotpedia survey he said that after the Army he taught high school and college and worked in the private sector.
Hamby was the Democratic nominee for District 100 in 2016, when incumbent Bryan Cutler (R) defeated him with 73.93% of the vote, and again in 2018, when Cutler won 72.0% to Hamby's 28.0%.
In his survey he said he was a Republican for 35 years and a Democrat for 15 before becoming an independent.
He said his priorities include on-time state budgets, taxation of petroleum pipelines as real property, and a moratorium on data center development in Pennsylvania.
